moisture_deficit.name: Root-zone Soil Moisture Deficit
moisture_deficit.scientific_rationale: Direct measure of water availability for crops; desiccation degrades microbial habitats and structure.
moisture_deficit.notes: Root-zone wetness fraction = 0.450. Deficit mapped from 0.75 (no stress) to 0.25 (acute stress).

precipitation_deficit.name: Meteorological Recharge Deficit (Moisture-Buffered)
precipitation_deficit.direction: Lower precipitation -> Higher recharge deficit; mitigated when root-zone moisture is adequate.
precipitation_deficit.scientific_rationale: Atmospheric recharge deficit. Buffered by root-zone soil water to prevent false drought alerts during irrigation.
precipitation_deficit.notes: 3-month rolling mean precip = 0.43 mm/day. Raw meteorological deficit = 100.0/100. Root-zone moisture (0.450) provides intermediate buffering (penalty multiplier: 0.83). Final buffered score = 83.33/100.

thermal_stress.name: Topsoil Thermal Stress
thermal_stress.scientific_rationale: High topsoil temperatures accelerate organic oxidation and elevate evaporative demand.
thermal_stress.notes: Topsoil temperature = 12.95 C. Stress mapped from 24.0 C (favorable) to 38.0 C (extreme thermal load).

soc_vulnerability.name: Static SOC Depletion Vulnerability
soc_vulnerability.scientific_rationale: Depleted organic carbon reduces aggregate stability, cation retention, and water holding capacity.
soc_vulnerability.notes: Static topsoil SOC baseline = 12.95 g/kg. Vulnerability scaled from 25.0 g/kg (high resilience) to 5.0 g/kg (depleted).

ph_deviation.name: Static pH Neutrality Deviation
ph_deviation.scientific_rationale: Deviations from neutrality trigger nutrient precipitation and micronutrient imbalances.
ph_deviation.notes: Static topsoil pH baseline = 6.55. Deviation from [6.5, 7.5] neutral window = 0.00 pH units.

risk_assessment.explanation: Record [2024-12] Index: 47.87/100 (Medium Risk). Dynamic Environmental Stress: 55.5/100; Static Baseline Soil Vulnerability: 30.1/100. Primary risk driver is 'Meteorological Recharge Deficit (Moisture-Buffered)' (sub-score: 83.3/100).

recommendations.title: Meteorological Recharge Deficit Mitigation & Rainwater Retention
recommendations.primary_intervention: Implement localized water retention to compensate for deficient precipitation recharge.
actionable_steps: Maintain in-field bunds and field boundaries to prevent surface runoff during sudden rain events.
Utilize farm pond or community rainwater catchment structures to supplement soil profiles.
Utilize moisture buffering from existing root-zone storage to stagger irrigation cycles.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Buffers against extended regional dry spells and protects groundwater tables.
recommendations.reason: Precipitation recharge deficit is 83.3/100 based on 3-month rolling rainfall trends.
recommendations.cost_category: Moderate Investment (Water Harvesting) / Low Cost (Furrow Diking)
recommendations.limitations: Rainwater retention structures require farm land allocation and earth-moving machinery.

recommendations.title: Deficit Irrigation Scheduling & Surface Cover Maintenance
recommendations.primary_intervention: Transition to high-efficiency moisture conservation irrigation.
actionable_steps: Maintain continuous crop residue cover across at least 30% of soil surface.
Prioritize drip irrigation or alternate-furrow irrigation over broad flood inundation.
Monitor weekly root-zone moisture depletion curves.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Maintains root-zone hydraulic conductivity and dampens agricultural drought vulnerability.
recommendations.reason: Root-zone moisture deficit is 60.0/100, constraining plant available water.
recommendations.limitations: Requires localized crop residue mulch availability; pressurized micro-irrigation requires capital equipment.

recommendations.title: Organic Matter Augmentation & Residue Retention
recommendations.primary_intervention: Increase organic inputs and adopt non-inversion conservation agriculture.
actionable_steps: Apply 5-8 tonnes/ha compost or vermicompost annually.
Rotate cereal crops with nodulating grain legumes (e.g. chickpea, moong) to enhance biological soil inputs.
Adopt reduced tillage to minimize organic carbon oxidation.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Progressively elevates topsoil SOC toward regional target (> 15.0 g/kg) and strengthens soil buffering.
recommendations.reason: Topsoil organic carbon vulnerability is 60.2/100, indicating low organic carbon buffering.
recommendations.limitations: Soil organic carbon elevation requires multi-season residue retention; not an immediate single-season fix.

recommendations.title: Favorable Thermal Regime Maintenance
recommendations.primary_intervention: Topsoil temperatures are within optimal biological ranges.
actionable_steps: Continue normal seasonal cultivation practices.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Sustains optimal conditions for biological nitrogen fixation and root respiration.
recommendations.reason: Topsoil thermal stress is 0.0/100, which accelerates evaporative loss and microbial heat stress.
recommendations.limitations: Surface shading provides 2-5°C canopy cooling but does not counteract regional macroclimate heatwaves alone.

recommendations.indicator_name: Soil pH Deviation from Optimal Neutral Band
recommendations.title: Optimal Soil pH Neutral Band Preservation
recommendations.primary_intervention: Soil reaction is within ideal agronomic neutral range (6.5 - 7.5).
actionable_steps: Continue standard balanced fertilizer management.
Conduct routine biennial soil pH testing to verify long-term stability.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Ensures maximum bioavailability of all essential macro- and micronutrients.
recommendations.reason: Soil pH deviation score is 0.0/100 (observed pH: 6.55), indicating mild chemical reaction deviation.
recommendations.limitations: Chemical amendments require precise dosage titration based on laboratory soil testing to prevent overcorrection.

dry_spell.scenario_description: Extended 30-day acute dry spell with zero precipitation and elevated ambient air temperatures.
dry_spell.resilience_assessment: Moderate buffering: Existing soil organic matter provides temporary structural water retention, damping initial acute desiccation.
assumptions: Assumes zero atmospheric precipitation over the entire 30-day projection horizon.
Assumes constant elevated 2m air temperature of 32.0 C (+3.0 C regional anomaly).
Atmospheric evaporative demand is sustained at high levels without precipitation replenishment.
Does not simulate subsurface irrigation, perched water tables, or capillary flux.
This is an exploratory HYPOTHETICAL SCENARIO for risk stress-testing and resilience analysis.
NO probability of occurrence, validation accuracy, or predictive confidence is assigned or claimed.
Operational numerical weather predictions do NOT offer deterministic skill at a 30-day horizon.
Atmospheric air temperature is NOT measured or simulated soil temperature.

heavy_rainfall.scenario_description: Active monsoon / atmospheric recharge pulse with high cumulative precipitation.
heavy_rainfall.resilience_assessment: Recharge pulse: Eliminates atmospheric recharge deficit but requires adequate surface drainage to prevent waterlogging and anaerobic root conditions.
assumptions: Assumes persistent high atmospheric precipitation of 15.0 mm/day (450 mm cumulative).
Assumes moderate 2m air temperature of 22.0 C during cloudy/rainy conditions.
Evaluates potential waterlogging and excess recharge scenarios.
